And all of a sudden, something strange appeared in the sky and they videotaped it and and reported it on the evening news.

discussion.text: Watkins announces in a press release that for 45 days from June 1, 2005 he will call down UFOs for the media over Las Vegas and that a spaceship will descend on his signal and sit in the sky for almost two days.

discussion.by: KTNV Channel 13 Las Vegas (reporter Mike Dello Stritto)
discussion.text: The station's crew meets Watkins at a time and place of their choosing in the last week of May 2005; two objects appear on camera, a white one and then an orange orb, and the footage runs on the evening news. The linked copy is the segment as it circulates today.

A second station tries the same thing days later from the driveway of Watkins' apartment and reports seeing only an airplane: 'We tried, it's a no-show.' The station's own page is gone; the words survive in a forum repost.
Bartholomew lists the explanations skeptics offered within two days (a model aircraft, a balloon, lasers, a concentrated light effect) and notes the site was near Nellis Air Force Base.

Malone says an anonymous site's weather-balloon theory has most likely 'got PY's UFOs pegged' and runs photos captioned as Watkins with weather balloons, adding that Watkins says the man in them is not him.

The reporter is quoted as having gone in expecting to ridicule the claim and come away believing he had seen an unidentified object; the station asked Nellis about aircraft and got no answer. Reported in a 2007 Wikipedia snapshot, the station's own page being gone.

Watkins says the spaceship would never have appeared if he had not been filmed calling it down, blames the Las Vegas media for refusing to film the promised descent, and demands 45 days of standby cameras.

The article offers as one explanation that Watkins signals a friend who releases balloons nearby during his meditation, and in the same breath calls this speculation with no evidence, since the crew chose the location.
Pritchett reports that Watkins' brother confirmed his death from a heart attack in August 2014, and says he is still not sure how Watkins pulled the summoning off.
SharpEye says the first object 'is very much a white balloon'; Duke says they look like balloons and asks whether the station was complicit.
The same poster says the second object gives him trouble: it seems to travel through the clouds and ascend vertically at speed.
Wolf reads the orange orb as a specular reflection of the sun from a distant aircraft, a shapeless blob when the angle is right.
Michels says people have since looked at the footage and said Watkins had an associate who released a balloon, adding that there is no evidence this happened and that it is an alternative hypothesis.

Same 1947 Kenneth Arnold sighting, but this telling claims the craft matched the Horten brothers' design, which recasts the object as a human-built craft.
Concerns paranormal experiences Arnold had after his 1947 sighting, as told in his daughter's book, not the sighting itself; that makes it a distinct story from the Arnold sighting.

Hypnosis tapes in which Puharich himself suggests the Nine. This tells the Nine coming through under hypnosis as Puharich's leading questions rather than real contact, which is a different core claim about the same kind of session.

Both say a program recruits young people from around the world. This telling says children from native cultures are recruited as psionic assets to lure UFOs, while the story says they are gathered to pilot craft at black facilities.
The Wall Street Journal explains the same 1967 Malmstrom missile shutdown as an EMP rather than a UFO, a competing core claim about the same event.
Both are about someone coming into Matt Gaetz's office to tell him about a hidden program. This telling says the visitor described psionic human cargo; the story says hybrid breeding.
Same 2024 New Jersey drone flap, but this telling claims the objects come from underwater, emerging off the coast.
Both concern what kind of evidence the Nimitz Tic Tac encounter gives. Madden treats it as testimony from reliable witnesses, while the story calls it multisensory evidence.

Both are about the Philadelphia Experiment. This telling says it really happened in Rhode Island and Philadelphia was the cover story, while the story calls the Philadelphia-to-Norfolk teleportation a bogus disinformation campaign.
Both concern the claimed alien base off Point Dume (Sycamore Knoll); the story asserts a base that was erased from maps, while this telling says there was no base.
The same 1947 Roswell crash, but this telling says the craft may have been human technology, while the story's tellings call it a bona fide UFO crash.
Both are about what the Shroud records of the man in it, but Strieber says it shows a body that had died and turned into light, while this telling says the man was alive.
Same 1975 Travis Walton abduction, but the core claim is different: Shermer says it was made up and points to a failed lie detector test.

Both concern UFOs appearing at nuclear sites, but this telling explains them as aliens under a prime directive waiting for humanity to become less violent, where the story explains them as future humans guarding their timeline.
Both are about the July 2019 USS Omaha sphere video off San Diego, but this telling explains it as an ordinary heat source dropping behind the horizon, not an anomalous craft.
